name: Sprocket
text: Implement a shadow test on the new prompt before a full rollout. This allows us to gather data on its performance without affecting the entire user base, minimizing risk while ensuring quality feedback. The trade-off is a longer timeline for full deployment, but this approach enhances our confidence in the prompt's effectiveness and reliability.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow testing only gives us a partial view of the prompt's performance, as it may not catch silent quality drops that users don't notice. A better approach might be to implement canary deployments with automated metrics tracking, which could provide more comprehensive insights into the prompt's impact. This would settle the argument if we could quantify the reduction in silent failures and measure the overall quality improvement against the added complexity of canary deployments.

name: Sprocket
text:
Run a 24-hour canary deployment to 5% of users with real-time quality and latency monitoring. This gives us live data on how the new prompt behaves under real load without risking the full user base. The trade-off is a small slice of users may see degraded performance if the prompt fails, but we catch it fast and roll back immediately. Shadow testing is safer but misses edge cases; canary deployments expose them.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: Canary deployments still miss silent failures—like a prompt that degrades answer quality without spiking latency or errors. A better alternative is to run a dual-prompt A/B test with forced user feedback collection, not just metrics. Settle it with a 48-hour trial where 10% of users get the new prompt and we measure both explicit ratings and hidden quality checks.
